Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo today — it was helpful to see Redwood's routing and quantization options. Per our call, the execs want a clear Mutual Action Plan so we can budget for procurement and schedule a two-week technical trial. High level asks we discussed:

- Benchmarks: 95th percentile latency and cost per 1M tokens for our baseline templates.
- Success criteria: response quality parity with our current vendor on entity extraction and hallucination rate < 1.5% on the test set.
- Model shortlist: a quantized medium/large model alternative plus a small low-latency option.
- Timeline: trial start mid-Jan, target procurement decision by end of Jan.

Can you share a draft MAP with milestones and who at Redwood will own each item (SE contact, tech onboarding, test dataset ingestion, test harness)? I've attached our initial prompt set stub for benchmarking.

Thanks — Evan

2) Test dataset ingestion + verification — target 2027-01-06 — Owner: HealthSpan (Evan / Mike) with Marissa support

I've also attached a preliminary benchmark matrix (benchmark-matrix-v1.xlsx) that Ben will populate with model slate runs once we confirm the targets and dataset.

Thanks, Olga / Evan — looping in more concrete benchmark specifics so we can get alignment before the trial. Below is my proposed technical acceptance matrix and the initial model shortlist we'll run during the trial window.

Benchmark success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end response time < 250ms for short templates (<= 120 tokens generation) on lowest acceptable instance class; p95 < 600ms for long templates (>= 512 token generates) for analysis workloads.
- Cost: target net inference cost <= $6.50 per 1M tokens (post-batching / with our standard 8-bit quantization path). If HealthSpan prefers a relative target, we can aim for at least 20% lower cost than current baseline.
- Quality: entity extraction exact-match >= 97% and hallucination rate <= 1.5% measured against the shared test set. For broader intent classification we aim for F1 >= 0.92.
- Reliability: < 0.2% token-drop/retry error rate during a 2-week trial window; at least 99.5% availability during scheduled runs.

Model slate (initial runs):
- Mistral-7B-instruct (8-bit quantized) — low-cost, low-latency candidate
- Llama-2-Chat-70B (int4 quantized variant) — higher-quality reference point for extraction tasks
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (q4_o) — mid/large model balance to evaluate cost/quality tradeoffs
- Redwood-curated small model (rw-small-2b-q8) — fallback low-latency option for production tails

Trial plan:
1) Smoke runs (Day 1): ingestion verification, ~100 samples across templates to sanity check outputs.
2) Full benchmark (Days 2-4): run entire prompt set across model slate at three concurrency points (1, 8, 32) to measure latency distribution and cost.
3) Quality sweep (Days 5-6): run evaluation harness for entity extraction and hallucination checks and produce PR/recall metrics.

Data & access notes: please upload the test set to the shared Drive folder (link in Olga's MAP) and share a temp S3 stub if you need to exercise private VPC ingest. We will emit a CSV of per-sample outputs plus a summary dashboard.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
